events.headline: Stanley Black & Decker raises EPS outlook after tariff refund boost

lifecycle.authority: Retained structured Lifecycle authority; Markdown and SQLite not read

providers.reason: Stanley Black & Decker delivered a massive Q3 beat with adjusted EPS of $2.31 versus $1.55 estimates. Even excluding one-time tariff refunds, organic sales grew 4% with significant operational margin expansion. The company raised its full-year EPS guidance and authorized a new $1 billion share repurchase program, signaling strong confidence in continued earnings power.
providers.risk: Near-term price exhaustion following an 11-15% single-day surge to new 52-week highs.

providers.reason: Adjusted EPS of $2.31 beat by $0.75, FY guidance rose to $5.95–$6.25, and shares hit a new 52-week high with Citi lifting its target to $140 Buy. Tools & Outdoor organic growth of 4% and 400bp EBITDA margin expansion reinforce the turnaround narrative.
providers.risk: About $0.67 of the beat came from one-off tariff refunds, and at ~$120 the stock trades above Goldman's $100 Neutral target, so disappointment risk is elevated.

providers.reason: Q3 adjusted EPS $2.31 vs ~$1.55 consensus, raised FY26 EPS guidance plus $1B buyback, 4% organic growth and margin expansion.
providers.risk: Beat aided by $0.67 tariff refund with reported sales down 1%, risking fade after ~14% spike.
